newsitem.title: DUBAI: Baku-UAE air freight business moves up a gear.
newsitem.headline: Baku-UAE air freight business moves up a gear.

text.p: A fast-growing oil sector coupled with strong outbound trader tourism in Azerbaijan is driving strong air freight business between Baku and the oil-rich United Arab Emirates, airline executives say.
"Baku is booming," said C.K. Joyson, station manager at Sharjah's Planet Travel and Tours, the agent for Baku-based Imair, one of the biggest operators in the Emirates to Baku.

"Since the demise of the Soviet Union, travel has been made easier for people (from the CIS) to Dubai. Moscow was the key destination, but now Baku is the major point in the CIS for cargo from Dubai," Emirates airline cargo revenue optimisation manager Pradeep Kumar said.
Emirates in June started a thrice weekly Airbus 300 passenger and cargo service between Dubai -- about 30 km from Sharjah -- to Baku. The aircraft has about 12 tonnes for cargo.

"There is major business and very good demand. We are basically focusing on commercial goods, a lot of them are for the oil industry, like equipment from the U.S., Europe and the Far East," Kumar added.
"About 60 percent of our cargo is tourist cargo, mostly electronics and textiles," Joyson told Reuters, adding the rest was oil field equipment.
Tourist cargo refers to goods bought in the UAE by Azeri visitors, who stock up mostly on cheap electronics and garments in the downtown souks in Sharjah and Dubai, often for re-sale back home.
"Individuals sometimes take 10-15 tonnes each, like cars and car spare parts," Joyson said.
Imair has four scheduled Ilyushin 76 cargo flights a week to Baku. It also operates three scheduled flights to Baku and one to nearby Gyandzha on Tupolev 154 aircraft.

Azerbaijan Airlines is an important operator on the route. Its Dubai cargo supervisor Nurid Aliav said there are four regular flights on Ilyushin 76 a week and they often put on extra chartered flights. The airline also operates three Boeing 727 passenger flights a week.
"Seventy to 80 percent of our cargo is tourist cargo, like electronics," Aliav said, but added that the airline also carries a large amount oil equipment.
"Flights to Baku are fuller than flights from Baku," Aliav said, adding his airline carries 140-150 tonnes weekly from Dubai.
"The plane arrives 95 percent empty," Joyson said, adding that those shipments were mainly oil industry equipment repairs.

Sharjah airport figures show exports to Baku reached 11,226 tonnes in 1996. To Gyandzha 944 tonnes were carried. In May this year, 739 tonnes moved from Sharjah to Baku. Fourteen tonnes moved in the other direction.
Dubai Cargo Village data show Dubai exported 4,014 tonnes to Baku in 1996 and imported only three tonnes. In the first five months of this year 2,537 tonnes moved from Dubai to Baku.
Rates to Baku range from $1.20 to $1.50 per kg.
"The current rate, which is lower because it is summer so there are fewer tourists, is $1.25," Aliav said. For over a tonne, the rate drops to $1.20.
Imair charges $1.35 for shipments of between 15 kg and two tonnes, $1.30 for two to five tonnes, $1.25 for five to ten tonnes and $1.20 for over 10 tonnes, Joyson said.
Emirates quotes around $1.50 on 100 kg shipments to Baku.
In addition to the regularly scheduled flights, other operators run unscheduled chartered flights to and from Baku. -- Dubai newsroom +9714-626990
